Ναασσών.long: Nahshon, son of Amminadab and father of Salmon, and one of the ancestors of Jesus.

νύξ.as:
νύξ, gen. νυκτός, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for לַיְלָה;]
night: Mt 12:40, Mk 6:48, Jo 13:30, al.; gen. temp. (of the time within which something happens; M, Pr., 73; B1., § 36, 13), νυκτός, by night, Mt 2:14, Jo 3:2, I Th 5:7, al.; ν. κ. ἡμέρας, Mk 5:5, I Th 2:9, al.; ἡμέρας κ. ν., Lk 18:7, Re 4:8, al.; μέσης ν., Mt 25:6; dat., νυκτί, in ans. to the question, "when?" (rare in cl.; Hdt., Soph.), ταύτῃ τ. ν., Lk 12:20, al.; ἐκείνῃ, Ac 12:6; ἐπιούσῃ, Ac 23:11; acc. durat. (Bl., § 34, 8; Kühner3, III, 314 b), ν. κ. ἠμέραν, Lk 2:37, Ac 20:31; τ. νύκτας, Lk 21:37; διὰ νυκτός (= cl. νυκτός; Bl., § 42, 1; 46, 7), Ac 5:1916:917:1023:31; δι’ ὅλης ν., Lk 5:5; κατὰ μέσον τῆς ν. (Bl., § 47, 6), Ac 27:27. Metaph.: Jo 9:4, Ro 13:12, I Th 5:5.

Ναζαρέτ.long: Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.
Ναζαρέτ.sd: Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine
Ναζαρέτ.as:
Ναζαρά
(Mt 4:13—L, -άθ—Lk 4:16), Ναζαρέθ (Mt 21:11, Ac 10:38), Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, indecl. (Semitic form uncertain),
Nazareth: Mt 2:23, Mk 1:9, Lk 1:262:4, 39, 51, Jo 1:45, 46.†

Ναζωραῖος.long: a Nazarene, an inhabitant of Nazareth.
Ναζωραῖος.sd: a Nazoræan, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth; by extension, a Christian
Ναζωραῖος.as:
Ναζωραῖος, -ου, ὁ
(= -ρηνός, q.v.),
a Nazarene: Mt 2:23(LXX)26:71, Lk 18:37, Jo 18:5, 719:19, Ac 2:223:64:106:1422:824:526:9.†

νηστεύω.as:
νηστεύω
(< νῆστις), [in LXX for צוּם;]
to fast (Arist., Aristoph., al.): Mt 4:26:16-189:14, 15, Mk 2:18-20, Lk 5:33-3518:12, Ac 13:2, 3.†

Ναζαρά.long: Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.
Ναζαρά.sd: Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine
Ναζαρά.as:
Ναζαρά
(Mt 4:13—L, -άθ—Lk 4:16), Ναζαρέθ (Mt 21:11, Ac 10:38), Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, indecl. (Semitic form uncertain),
Nazareth: Mt 2:23, Mk 1:9, Lk 1:262:4, 39, 51, Jo 1:45, 46.†

νόσος.sd: a malady (rarely figuratively, of moral disability)
νόσος.as:
νόσος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX for חֳלִי, etc.;]
disease, sickness: Mt 4:23, 248:17(Aq.)9:3510:1, Mk 1:34, Lk 4:406:177:219:1, Ac 19:12.†
SYN.: v.s. ἀσθένεια.

νομίζω.long: I practice, hold by custom; I deem, think, consider, suppose.
νομίζω.sd: properly, to do by law (usage), i.e. to accustom (passively, be usual); by extension, to deem or regard
νομίζω.as:
** νομίζω
(< νόμος), [in LXX: Wi 13:217:3, Si 29:4, II Mac4, IV Mac8*;]
1.to practise, hold by custom: Ac 16:13 (Rec., but v. infr.).
2.to deem, consider, suppose: Mt 5:1710:3420:10, Lk 2:443:23, Ac 7:258:2014:1916:13, 2717:2921:29, I Co 7:26, 36, I Ti 6:5.†
SYN.: ἡγέομαι, q.v.

νόμος.long: usage, custom, law; in NT: of law in general, plur: of divine laws; of a force or influence impelling to action; of the Mosaic law; meton: of the books which contain the law, the Pentateuch, the Old Testament scriptures in general.
νόμος.sd: law (through the idea of prescriptive usage), genitive case (regulation), specially, (of Moses (including the volume); also of the Gospel), or figuratively (a principle)
νόμος.der: from a primary (to parcel out, especially food or grazing to animals);
νόμος.as:
νόμος, -ου, ὁ
(< νέμω, to deal out, distribute), [in LXX chiefly for תּוֹרָה, also for חֻקָּה, etc.;]
that which is assigned, hence, usage, custom, then law; in NT (only in Mt, Jo, Ja, and the Lucan and Pauline bks.);
1. of law in general: Ro 3:275:13b; pl., of divine laws, He 8:1010:16; ὁ ν. τ. Χριστοῦ, Ga 6:2; (τ.) ἐλευθερίας, Ja 1:252:12; βασιλικιός (Hort., in l.; Deiss., LAE, 3673), Ja 2:8.
2. Of a force or influence impelling to action: Ro 7:21, 23a, 258:2.
3. Of the Mosaic law: Mt 5:18, Lk 2:27, Jo 1:17, Ac 6:13, Ro 2:15, I Co 9:8, I Ti 1:8, He 7:19, al.; ν. Μωυσέως, Lk 2:22, Jo 7:23, Ac 15:5, al.; κυρίου, Lk 2:39; κατὰ τὸν ν., Ac 22:12, He 7:59:22.
4. Anarthrous (Bl., § 46, 8; ICC on Ro 2:12, 13), νόμος,
(a) of law in general: Ro 2:12, 14b3:20, 214:15, al.;
(b) of the Mosaic law in its quality as law: Ro 2:14a5:2010:4, Ga 2:19, al.; οἱ ἐκ ν., Ro 4:14; ὑπὸ νόμον, I Co 9:20, Ga 4:5; ν. πράσσειν (πληροῦν), Ro 2:2513:8.
5. Of Christian teaching: ν. πίστεως, Ro 3:27; τ. Χριστοῦ, Ga 6:2.
6. By meton., of the books which contain the law;
(a) of the Pentateuch: Mt 12:5, Jo 1:45, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ οἱ προφῆται, Mt 5:17, Lk 16:16, al.; ὁ ν. καὶ προφῆται κ. ψαλμοί, Lk 24:44;
(b) of the OT Scriptures in general (as Heb. תּוֹרָה): Jo 10:3412:3415:25, I Co 14:21, al.

ναί.kj: even so, surely, truth, verily, yea, yes
ναί.der: a primary particle of strong affirmation;
ναί.as:
ναί,
particle of affirmation,
yea, verily, even so; in answer to a question: Mt 9:2813:5117:2521:16, Jo 11:2721:15, 16, Ac 5:822:27, Ro 3:29; seq. λέγω ὑμῖν, Mt 11:9, Lk 7:26; repeated for emphasis, ναὶ ναί (opp. to οὒοὔ): Mt 5:37; ἤτω ὑμῶν τὸ ναὶ ναί, Ja 5:12; ν. καὶ οὔ, II Co 1:18, 19; ἵνα ᾖ . . . τὸ ναὶ ναί, II Co 1:17; τὸ ν., II Co 1:20; in assent to an assertion: Mt 15:27, Mk 7:28, Re 14:1316:7; in confirmation of a previous assertion: Mt 11:26, Lk 10:2111:5112:5, Phl 4:3, Phm 20; in solemn asseveration: Re 1:722:20.†

νίπτω.long: I wash; mid. I wash my own (hands, etc.).
νίπτω.sd: to cleanse (especially the hands or the feet or the face); ceremonially, to perform ablution
νίπτω.as:
νίπτω, late form of νίζω,
[in LXX chiefly for רחץ;]
to wash, usually of a part of the body: c. acc. pers., Jo 13:8; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:5, 6, 8, 12, 14, I Ti 5:10; mid., reflexive, to wash oneself: Jo 9:7, 11, 15; τ. χεῖρας, Mt 15:2, Mk 7:3; τ. πόδας, Jo 13:10; τ. πρόσωπον, Mt 6:17 (in cl. Att. prose, used only in compounds; cf. ἀπο-νίπτω).†
SYN.: λούω (q.v.), πλύνω.

νήθω.as:
νήθω,
[in LXX for טָוָה, שׁזר hoph., Ex 26:3135:25, al.;]
to spin: Mt 6:28, Lk 12:27.†

νεκρός.long: (a) adj: dead, lifeless, subject to death, mortal, (b) noun: a dead body, a corpse.
νεκρός.sd: dead (literally or figuratively; also as noun)
νεκρός.as:
νεκρός, -ά, -όν,
[in LXX chiefly for מֵתpossible misspelling of מָוֶת;]
dead,
I. as adj.,
1. prop.: Ac 5:1020:9, Ja 2:26, Re 1:18, al.; ὡσεὶ ν., Mt 28:4, Mk 9:26, Re 1:17; of that which is subject to death, Ro 8:10.
2. Metaph.,
(a) of persons: Lk 15:24, 32; of those immersed in worldly cares, Mt 8:22, Lk 9:60; of spiritual death, Jo 5:25, Ro 6:13, Eph 5:14, Re 3:1; τ. παραπτώμασιν, Eph 2:1, 5, Col 2:13; of the opposite condition, ν. τῇ ἁμαρτίᾳ, Ro 6:11;
(b) of things regarded as inoperative, devoid of power: ἁμαρτία, Ro 7:8; πίστις, Ja 2:17, 26; ἔργα, He 6:19:14.
II. As subst., νεκρός, ὁ (Hom., al.), chiefly in pl. (οἱ) ν., the dead: Mt 11:5, Mk 12:26, Lk 20:37, I Co 15:15, al.; ἀνάστασις (τ.) νεκρῶν, Mt 22:31, Ac 17:32, al.; ν. . . . ζῶντες, Mt 22:32, Mk 12:27, Ac 10:42, al.; ἀπὸ νεκρῶν, Lk 16:30; ἐκ ν., Mk 6:14, Lk 24:46, Jo 12:1, Ac 13:34, Ro 10:7, al.; πρωτότοκος ἐκ τῶν ν., Col 1:18; ζωὴ ἐκ ν., Ro 11:15; constr. praegn., ἐκ ν. ζῶντες, Ro 6:13.

νυμφών.as:
**† νυμφών, -ῶνος, ὁ
(< νύμφη), [in LXX: To 6:13, 16*;]
the bride-chamber (Heb. חֻפָּה, LXX, παστός, Ps 18 (19):5, Jl 2:16): Mt 22:10 (WH; γάμος, RV); οἱ υἱοὶ τοῦ ν. (cf. cl. νυμφαγωγός, νυμφευτής), the bridegroom's friends who have charge of the nuptial arrangements: Mt 9:15, Mk 2:19, Lk 5:34.†

νυμφίος.as:
νυμφίος, -ου, ὁ
(< νύμφη), [in LXX for חָתָן;]
a bridegroom: Mt 9:1525:1, 5, 6, 10, Mk 2:19, 20, Lk 5:34, 35, Jo 2:93:29, Re 18:23.†

νέος.sd: "new", i.e. (of persons) youthful, or (of things) fresh; figuratively, regenerate
νέος.der: including the comparative ; a primary word;
νέος.as:
νέος, -α, -ον,
[in LXX for נַעַר (Ge 37:2, Ex 33:11, al.), חָדָשׁ (Le 23:16, Nu 28:26, al.), etc.; compar. -ώτερος for קָטֹן, צָעִיר, etc.;]
1.young, youthful: Tit 2:4.
2.new (prop., in respect of time; v.s. καινός): οἶνος (cf. οἶ. καινός, Mt 26:29), Mt 9:17, Mk 2:22, Lk 5:37-[39]; φύραμα (fig.), I Co 5:7; διαθήκη (cf. καινὴ δ., He 9:15), He 12:24; metaph., ἄνθρωπος (cf. καινὸς ἀ, Eph 2:15), Col 3:10.
3. Compar., -ώτερος, -α, -ον, younger: Lk 15:12, 1322:26, Jo 21:18; pl., οἱ ν., Ac 5:6 (Rackham, in l.), I Ti 5:11, Tit 2:6; opp. to πρεσβύτεροι, I Ti 5:1, I Pe 5:5; αἱ ν., I Ti 5:2, 14.
4.Νέα Πόλις, Neapolis: Ac 16:11 (Rec., Νεάπολις, q.v.)
SYN.: καινός, q.v.

νύμφη.long: (a) a bride, young wife, young woman, (b) a daughter-in-law.
νύμφη.sd: compare Latin "nupto," to marry); a young married woman (as veiled), including a betrothed girl; by implication, a son's wife
νύμφη.der: from a primary but obsolete verb (to veil as a bride;
νύμφη.as:
νύμφη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX chiefly for כַּלָּה;]
1. cl., a bride, young wife, young woman: Mt 25:1, WH, mg., Jo 3:29, Re 18:2321:2, 922:17.
2. As freq. in LXX (Ge 38:11, al., for כַּלָּה;
(a)bride;
(b)daughter-in-law) and in MGr. (νύφφη, νύφη), a daughter-in-law: Mt 10:35, Lk 12:53.†

νήπιος.long: unlearned, unenlightened; noun: an infant, child.
νήπιος.sd: not speaking, i.e. an infant (minor); figuratively, a simple-minded person, an immature Christian
νήπιος.der: from an obsolete particle (implying negation) and G2031 (ἔπος);
νήπιος.as:
νήπιος, -α, -ον,
[in LXX chiefly for עוֹלֵל, also for פְּתִי, etc.;]
infant; of children and minors: Mt 21:16(LXX), I Co 13:11, Ga 4:1 (v. Lft., in l.). Metaph., childish, unskilled, simple (Ps 18 (19):8, Pr 1:32, al.): Mt 11:25, Lk 10:21, Ro 2:20, Ga 4:3, Eph 4:14, I Th 2:7 (WH, fox ἤπιοι); opp. to τέλειος, He 5:13; ν. ἐν Χριστῷ, I Co 3:1.†

νῖκος.as:
† νῖκος, -ους, τό, late form of νίκη,
[in LXX: La 3:18 (נֶצַח), I Es 3:9, II Mac 10:38, IV Mac 17:12; εἰς ν. (instead of εἰς τέλος, Jb 14:20), II Ki 2:26, Jb 36:7, Am 1:118:7, Je 3:5, La 5:20 (לָנֶצֵח, as נ׳ in Syr., = victory)*;]
victory: Mt 12:20 (Is 42:3, LXX ἀλήθεια), I Co 15:54 (Is 25:8, Aq., Th.), I Co 15:55 (Ho 13:14, LXX δίκη), I Co 15:57.†

Νινευίτης.long: a Ninevite, an inhabitant of Nineveh, a city on the Tigris in Assyria.
Νινευίτης.sd: a Ninevite, i.e. inhabitant of Nineveh
Νινευίτης.as:
Νινευείτης (Rec. -ευίτης, L, -ΐτης), -ου, ὁ,
a Ninevite: Mt 12:41, Lk 11:30, 32.†

νότος.sd: the south(-west) wind; by extension, the southern quarter itself
νότος.as:
νότος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX chiefly for נֶגֶב, also for דָּרוֹם, תֵּימָן and קָדִים;]
1. prop., the south wind: Lk 12:55, Ac 27:1328:13.
2.South: Lk 13:29, Re 21:13.
3.the South, as a region (cf. נֶגֶב): Mt 12:42, Lk 11:31.†

νοέω.long: I understand, think, consider, conceive, apprehend; aor. possibly: realize.
νοέω.sd: to exercise the mind (observe), i.e. (figuratively) to comprehend, heed
νοέω.as:
νοέω-ῶ
(< νοῦς), [in LXX chiefly for בּין, also for שׂכל hi., etc;]
1.to perceive with the mind, understand (for the phrase νοῶν κ. φρονῶν, in wills, v. MM, xvii): absol., Mt 16:9, Mk 8:17; c. acc., Eph 3:4, I Ti 1:7; c. dat. instr., τ. καρδίᾳ, Jo 12:40; pass., Ro 1:20; seq. ὅτι, Mt 15:1716:11, Mk 7:18; c. acc. et inf., He 11:8.
2.to think, consider: absol., Mt 24:15, Mk 13:14, Eph 3:20; c. acc. rei, II Ti 2:7. (cf. -εὐ, κατα-, μετα-, προ-, ὑπο-νοέω).†

νῆστις.sd: not eating, i.e. abstinent from food (religiously)
νῆστις.der: from the inseparable negative particle (not) and G2068 (ἐσθίω);
νῆστις.as:
νῆστις, -ιος, ὁ, ἡ
(< νη-, neg. prefix, + ἐσθίω),in cl., chiefly poët., [in LXX: Da LXX 6:18 (19) (טְוָת)*;]
not eating, fasting: Mt 15:32, Mk 8:3.†

νεφέλη.as:
νεφέλη, -ης, ἡ
(< νέφος), [in LXX chiefly for עָנָן, also for עָב, etc.;]
a cloud (single and specific as opp. to νέφος, a great indefinite mass of vapour): Mt 17:524:3026:64, Mk 9:713:2614:62, Lk 9:34, 3512:5421:37, Ac 1:9, I Th 4:17, Ju 12, Re 1:710:111:1214:14-16; of the pillar of cloud in the wilderness (Ex 14:19, 20, Ps 104:39, al.): I Co 10:1, 2.†

νεανίσκος.long: a young man, youth, an attendant.
νεανίσκος.as:
νεανίσκος, -ου, ὁ
(dimin. of νεανίας), [in LXX chiefly for נַעַר, also for בָּחוּר, etc.;]
a young man, youth: Mt 19:20, 22, Mk 14:5116:5, Lk 7:14, Ac 2:17(LXX)23:18, 22, I Jo 2:13, 14; of an attendant (cf. Ge 14:24, al.): Ac 5:10.†

Ναζαρέθ.long: Nazareth, a city of Galilee, where Jesus lived before His ministry.
Ναζαρέθ.sd: Nazareth or Nazaret, a place in Palestine
Ναζαρέθ.as:
Ναζαρά
(Mt 4:13—L, -άθ—Lk 4:16), Ναζαρέθ (Mt 21:11, Ac 10:38), Ναζαρέτ (so always Rec.; WH, in foll, instances, where -έθ, T), ἡ, indecl. (Semitic form uncertain),
Nazareth: Mt 2:23, Mk 1:9, Lk 1:262:4, 39, 51, Jo 1:45, 46.†

νόμισμα.sd: what is reckoned as of value (after the Latin numisma), i.e. current coin
νόμισμα.as:
νόμισμα, -τος, τό
(< νομίζω), [in LXX: Es 8:36 (דָּת), Ne 7:71 R (דַּרְכְּמוֹן), I Mac 15:6*;]
1.that which is established by usage, a custom.
2.The current coin of a state: Mt 22:19.†

νομικός.g: about law, one learned in the Law
νομικός.long: (a) adj: connected with law, about law, (b) noun: a lawyer, one learned in the Law, one learned in the Old Testament.
νομικός.sd: according (or pertaining) to law, i.e. legal (ceremonially); as noun, an expert in the (Mosaic) law
νομικός.as:
** νομικός, -ή, -όν
(< νόμος), [in LXX: IV Mac 5:4*;]
1.relating to law: μάχαι, Tit 3:9.
2.learned in the law; as subst., ὁ ν. (EV, lawyer): Mt 22:35, Lk 10:25, Tit 3:13; pl., Lk 7:3011:45, 46, 5214:3 (cf. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v.

ναός.long: a temple, a shrine, that part of the temple where God himself resides.
ναός.as:
ναός, -οῦ, ὁ,
(Att. νεώς; < ναίω, to inhabit), [in LXX (νεώς, II Mac 6:2, al.) chiefly for הֵיכָל;]
1.a temple (Hom., Pind., al.).
2. The inmost part of a temple, the shrine (Hdt., Xen., al.); in NT,
(a) generally: pl., Ac 17:24; of silver models of a heathen shrine, Ac 19:24;
(b) of the temple building proper, or sanctuary, at Jerusalem, as distinct from τ. ἱερόν (q.v.), the whole temple enclosure: Mt 23:16, 17, 3527:5, 40, Mk 14:5815:29, Jo 2:19, 20, Re 11:2; (τοῦ) θεοῦ, Mt 26:6127:51, Mk 15:38, Lk 1:9, 21, 2223:45, I Co 3:17, II Co 6:16, II Th 2:4, Re 11:1; of the temple in the Apocal. visions, Re 3:127:1511:1914:15, 1715:5, 6, 816:1, 1721:22a. Metaph., of Christians, I Co 3:166:19, II Co 6:16, Eph 2:21; of Christ's body, Jo 2:21 (cf. Jo 2:19); ὁ θεὸς ν. αὐτῆς ἐστιν, Re 21:22b.†
SYN.: ἱερόν.

νοσσίον.g: a nestling, the young of birds
νοσσίον.long: a nestling, the young of birds.
νοσσίον.as:
νοσσίον, -ου, τό, dimin. of νοσσός, q.v.,
[in LXX: Ps 83 (84):3 (אֶפְרֹחַ)*;]
a young bird: Mt 23:37.†

νῦν.long: adv. (a) of time: just now, even now; just at hand, immediately, (b) of logical connection: now then, (c) in commands and appeals: at this instant.
νῦν.sd: "now" (as adverb of date, a transition or emphasis); also as noun or adjective present or immediate
νῦν.kj: henceforth, + hereafter, of late, soon, present, this (time)
νῦν.der: a primary particle of present time;
νῦν.as:
νῦν, adv.,
[in LXX chiefly for עַתָּה;]
1. prop., of time, now, i.e. at the present time: as opp. to past, Jo 4:18, Ac 7:52, Ro 13:11, II Co 7:9, Col 1:24, al.; opp. to fut., Jo 12:27, Ro 11:31, al.; c. art., ὁ (ἡ, τὸ) et subst., the present: Ro 3:26, Ga 4:25, I Ti 6:17, Tit 2:12, al.; ἀπὸ τοῦ ν. (LXX for מֵעַתָּה), Lk 1:48, Ac 18:6, al.; ἄχρι τοῦ ν., Ro 8:22, Phl 1:5; ἕως τοῦ ν. (LXX for עַתָּה עַד), Mt 24:21, Mk 13:19; τὰ ν., as regards the present, Ac 5:38; c. pret., just now, but now, Mt 26:65, Jo 11:821:10; c. fut., now, presently, Jo 12:31, Ac 20:22; so c. praes., presently, forthwith, Jo 12:3117:13; καὶ ν., Jo 11:2217:5, al.; ἀλλὰ ν., Lk 22:36; ἔτι ν., I Co 3:2; τότε (πότε) . . . ν. (δέ), Ro 6:2111:30; ν. ἤδη, I Jo 4:3; ν. οὖν, Ac 10:33, al.
2. Of logical sequence (often difficult to disting. from the temporal sense; cf. Lft., Notes, 113 f.), now, therefore, now, however, as it is: Lk 11:39; καὶ ν., Ac 3:17, II Th 2:6, I Jo 2:28; id. seq. δεῦρο, Ac 7:34; ν. δέ, Jo 8:409:4115:22, 2418:36, I Co 5:117:1412:20, al. (cf. WM, 57911).

Νῶε.as:
Νῶε
(as LXX, FlJ, who also gives Νώεος, Νῶχος), ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נֹחַ),
Noah: Mt 24:37, 38, Lk 3:3617:26, 27, He 11:7, I Pe 3:20, II Pe 2:5.†

νυστάζω.g: I nod in sleep, am drowsy, slumber
νυστάζω.long: I nod in sleep, am drowsy, slumber.
νυστάζω.sd: to nod, i.e. (by implication) to fall asleep; figuratively, to delay
νυστάζω.der: from a presumed derivative of G3506 (νεύω);
νυστάζω.as:
νυστάζω
(cf. νεύω), [in LXX for נוּם, etc;]
to nod in sleep, fall asleep: Mt 25:5. Metaph., of negligence or delay, ἡ ἀπώλεια αὐτῶν οὐ νυστάζει (cf. Ps 120 (121):4, Is 5:27): II Pe 2:3.†

Ναζαρηνός.sd: a Nazarene, i.e. inhabitant of Nazareth
Ναζαρηνός.as:
Ναζαρηνός, -οῦ, ὁ,
(on the Semitic form, v. Dalman, Gr., 141 n.),
a Nazarene: Mk 1:2410:4714:6716:6, Lk 4:3424:19.†

νεότης.as:
νεότης, -ητος, ἡ
(< νέος), [in LXX chiefly for נְעוּרִים;]
youth: Mk 10:20, Lk 18:21, Ac 26:4, I Ti 4:12.†

νουνεχῶς.sd: in a mind-having way, i.e. prudently
νουνεχῶς.der: adverb from a comparative of the accusative case of G3563 (νοῦς) and G2192 (ἔχω);

νάρδος.long: spikenard, a perfume made originally from a plant growing on the Himalayas.
νάρδος.as:
νάρδος, -ου, ἡ
(Heb. נֵרְדְּ, both from Sanscrit narda, v. Boisacq, s.v.), [in LXX: Ca 1:124:13, 14 (נֵרְדְּ)*;]
nard;
(a) an Indian plant, the Nardostachys nardus jatamansi, used for the preparation of a fragrant ointment;
(b)ointment of nard: Mk 14:3, Jo 12:3.†

νοσσός.long: a young bird, nestling; a young one.
νοσσός.as:
νοσσός (νεοσσός, Rec., as in cl. Att. -ττός; Phryn. rejects the dissyl. form), -οῦ, ὁ
(< νέος), [in LXX chiefly for בֵּן;]
a young bird: Lk 2:24(LXX).†

νηστεία.sd: abstinence (from lack of food, or voluntary and religious); specially, the fast of the Day of Atonement
νηστεία.as:
νηστεία, -ας, ἡ
(< νηστεύω), [in LXX for צוֹם;]
fasting, a fast;
(a) of voluntary abstinence from food: Mt 17:21 (WH, R, txt., om.), Mk 9:29 (WH, txt., R, txt., om.), Lk 2:37, Ac 14:23; of the Day of Atonement, Ac 27:9;
(b) of involuntary abstinence: II Co 6:511:27.†
SYN.: ἀσιτία, q.v.

Ναγγαί.long: Naggai, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

Ναθάμ.long: Nathan, son of David, and an ancestor of Jesus.

Ναχώρ.long: Nahor, one of the ancestors of Jesus.

νομοδιδάσκαλος.g: a teacher and interpreter of the Mosaic Law
νομοδιδάσκαλος.long: a teacher and interpreter of the Mosaic Law.
νομοδιδάσκαλος.sd: an expounder of the (Jewish) law, i.e. a Rabbi
νομοδιδάσκαλος.as:
*† νομο-διδάσκαλος, -ου, ὁ,
a teacher of the law: Lk 5:17, Ac 5:34, I Ti 1:7 (NT and eccl. only; cf. νομοδείκτης, -διδάκτης, Plut.).†
SYN.: γραμματεύς, q.v.

Ναΐν.long: Nain, a city south-west of the Sea of Galilee.
Ναΐν.as:
Ναίν (Rec. Ναΐν), ἡ, indecl. (Heb. נָאִין),
Nain, a village of Galilee: Lk 7:11.†

νικάω.long: I conquer, am victorious, overcome, prevail, subdue.
νικάω.kj: conquer, overcome, prevail, get the victory
νικάω.as:
νικάω, -ῶ
(< νίκη), [in LXX: Ps 50 (51):4 (זכה), Pr 6:25 freq. (חמד); freq. in IV Mac;]
to conquer, prevail: absol., of Christ, Re 3:216:2; c. inf., Re 5:5; of Christians, Re 2:7, 11, 17, 263:5, 12, 2121:7; seq. ἐκ (RV, come victorious from), Re 15:2; as law-term (cl.), Ro 3:4(LXX); c. acc. pers., Lk 11:22, Re 11:713:7 ([WH], R, mg., om.); of Christ, Jo 16:33 (τ. κόσμον), Re 17:14; of Christians, I Jo 4:4; τ. πονηρόν, I Jo 2:13, 14; αὐτόν (ref. to ὁ κατήγωρ, ib. 2:10), Re 12:11; c. acc. rei, τὸν κόσμον, Jo 16:33, I Jo 5:4, 5; τὸ κακόν, Ro 12:21; pass., μὴ νικῶ ὑπὸ τ. κακοῦ, ib. (cf. ὑπερ-νικάω).†

νοσσιά.as:
νοσσιά, -ᾶς, ἡ
(< νοσσός), late form of cl., νεοσσιά, [in LXX chiefly for קֵן;]
1.a nest of birds.
2.a brood of young birds: Lk 13:34.†

νοῦς.long: the mind, the reason, the reasoning faculty, intellect.
νοῦς.sd: the intellect, i.e. mind (divine or human; in thought, feeling, or will); by implication, meaning
νοῦς.der: probably from the base of G1097 (γινώσκω);
νοῦς.as:
νοῦς
(contr. from νόος),ὁ, gen., dat., νοός, νοΐ (late forms, = cl., νοῦ, νῷ; Bl., § 9, 3), acc., νοῦν, [in LXX chiefly for לֵב, לֵבָב;]
1. prop., of the ruling faculty, mind, understanding, reason (v. Lft., Notes, 88 f.; Vaughan on Ro 7:23): Lk 24:45, Ro 1:287:2312:214:5, Eph 4:17, 23, Phl 4:7, II Th 2:2, I Ti 6:5, II Ti 3:8, Tit 1:15, Re 13:1817:9; ν. τ. σαρκός (ICC, in l.), Col 2:18; opp. to σάρξ, Ro 7:25; to πνεῦμα, I Co 14:14, 15; to γλῶσσα, I Co 14:19.
2. By meton., of an act of mind, a mind, thought, purpose: Ro 11:34 = I Co 2:16 (LXX), I Co 1:10.†
SYN.: v.s. πνεῦμα.

Ναθαναήλ.long: Nathanael, of Cana in Galilee, an early disciple, probably to be identified with Bartholomew.
Ναθαναήλ.sd: Nathanaël (i.e. Nathanel), an Israelite and Christian
Ναθαναήλ.as:
Ναθαναήλ, ὁ, indecl. (Heb. נְתַנְאֵל),
Nathanael, prob. to be identified with Bartholomew (q.v.): Jo 1:45-4921:2.†

Νικόδημος.long: Nicodemus, a member of the Sanhedrin.
Νικόδημος.sd: victorious among his people; Nicodemus, an Israelite
Νικόδημος.as:
Νικόδημος, -ου, ὁ,
Nicodemus: Jo 3:1, 4, 97:5019:39.†

νομή.sd: pasture, i.e. (the act) feeding (figuratively, spreading of a gangrene), or (the food) pasturage
νομή.der: feminine from the same as G3551 (νόμος);
νομή.as:
νομή, -ῆς, ἡ
(< νέμω, to pasture), [in LXX chiefly for מִרְעֶה, also for נָוֶה, etc.;]
1.a pasture, pasturage: fig., Jo 10:9.
2.a grazing, feeding; metaph., of a spreading sore, II Ti 2:17 (Polyb.).†

νιπτήρ.long: a basin for washing hands or feet.

νεύω.long: I nod, make a sign, beckon.
νεύω.as:
νεύω,
[in LXX: Pr 4:521:1*;]
to nod or beckon, as a sign : c. dat. pers. et inf., Jo 13:24, Ac 24:10 (cf. δια-, ἐκ-, ἐν-, ἐπι-, κατα-νεύω).†

νύσσω.as:
** νύσσω
(Att. -ττω), [in LXX: Si 22:19, III Mac 5:14*;]
to pierce: τ. πλευρὰν λόγχῃ, Jo 19:34, [Mt 27:49], WH.†

νοσφίζομαι.long: I rob; mid: I set apart for myself, appropriate for my own benefit, purloin.
νοσφίζομαι.sd: to sequestrate for oneself, i.e. embezzle
νοσφίζομαι.as:
νοσφίζω
(< νόσφι, apart, aside), [in LXX: Jos 7:1 (לקח), II Mac 4:32*;]
1. in Hom., as depon., to turn away (from), abandon.
2. After Hom., in act., to set apart, remove. Mid., to set apart for oneself, peculate, purloin: absol., Tit 2:10 (for ex. in π., v. MM, xvii); seq. ἀπό, Ac 5:2, 3.†

Νικόλαος.sd: victorious over the people; Nicolaus, a heretic

νεανίας.long: a young man, youth; a man in his prime (used even of a man of 40).
νεανίας.sd: a youth (up to about forty years)
νεανίας.as:
νεανίας, -ου, ὁ
(< νεάν = νέος), [in LXX for נַעַר, בָּחוּר;]
a young man: Ac 7:5820:923:17, 18.†

νῆσος.der: probably from the base of G3491 (ναῦς);
νῆσος.as:
νῆσος, -ου, ὁ,
[in LXX for אִי;]
an island: Ac 13:627:2628:1, 7, 9, 11, Re 1:96:1416:20.†

νεωκόρος.sd: a temple-servant, i.e. (by implication) a votary
νεωκόρος.der: from a form of G3485 (ναός) and (to sweep);
νεωκόρος.as:
* νεω-κόρος, -ου,
a temple-keeper; as honorary title given to a city (v. DB, i, 722 b): Ac 19:35.†

νουθετέω.sd: to put in mind, i.e. (by implication) to caution or reprove gently
νουθετέω.as:
νουθετέω, -ῶ
(< νοῦς, τίθημι, hence, put in mind), [in LXX: I Ki 3:13 (כּהה pi.), Jb8 (יסר pi., בִּין), Wi 11:1012:2, 26*;]
to admonish, exhort: c. acc. pers., Ac 20:31, Ro 15:14, I Co 4:14, Col 1:283:16, I Th 5:12, 14, II Th 3:15.†

νυνί.long: adv. (a) of time: just now, even now; just at hand, immediately, (b) of logical connection: now then, (c) in commands and appeals: at this instant.
νυνί.der: a prolonged form of G3568 (νῦν) for emphasis;
νυνί.as:
νυνί, an Attic strengthened form of νῦν
(in cl. always of time, and most often strictly of the pres.), [in LXX : Jb5, Pss2, II, IV Mac4, Ep. Je.*;]
now;
1. of time: c. praes., Ac 24:13, Ro 15:23, 25, I Co 13:13, II Co 8:11, 22, Phm 9, 11; c. pf., Ro 3:21; c. pret., Ro 6:2211:30 (WH, mg.) 7:6, Eph 2:13, Col 1:213:8; ἡ ν. ἀπολογία, Ac 22:1.
2. Of logical sequence (not so in cl.): Ro 7:17, I Co 5:11 (νῦν, WH) 12:18 (νῦν, WH, txt.) 15:20, He 8:6 (νῦν, WH, txt.), He 9:26 (cf. WM, 24, 579n).†

ναύκληρος.long: a captain (master) of a ship, ship-owner.
ναύκληρος.as:
* ναύ-κληρος, -ου, ὁ
(< ναῦς, κλῆρος),
a shipowner, shipmaster: Ac 27:11.†

νησίον.as:
*† νησίον, -ου, τό
(dimin. of νῆσος), = νησίς (Hdt., Thuc., al.),
a small island: Ac 27:16.†

ναύτης.as:
** ναύτης, -ου, ὁ
(< ναῦς), [in Aq.: Ez 27:9; Sm.: Ez 27:29*;]
a seaman, sailor: Ac 27:27, 30, Re 18:17.†

ναῦς.as:
ναῦς, νεώς acc. ναῦν, ἡ,
[in LXX for אֳנִי, אֲנִיָּה;]
a ship: Ac 27:41 (elsewhere in NT always τ. πλοῖον; v. M, Pr., 25 f.; Bl., Gosp., 186 f.).†

νεκρόω.g: I put to death, render weak
νεκρόω.long: lit. and met: I put to death, make as dead; I render weak, impotent.
νεκρόω.as:
*† νεκρόω, ῶ
(< νεκρός),
to make dead, put to death; pass., to be dead: hyperbolically, of impotent age, He 11:12; σῶμα, Ro 4:19. Trop., of carnal impulses, τὰ μέλη, Col 3:5.†

νέκρωσις.long: (a) putting to death, (b) dead or lifeless condition.
νέκρωσις.as:
*† νέκρωσις, -εως, ἡ
(< νεκρόω),
1.a putting to death.
2.a state of death, death: Ro 4:19, II Co 4:10 (v. Deiss., LAE, 94).†

νομοθεσία.sd: legislation (specially, the institution of the Mosaic code)
νομοθεσία.as:
** νομοθεσία, -ας, ἡ
(< νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: II Mac 6:23, IV Mac 5:3517:16*;]
legislation, lawgiving: Ro 9:4.†

νῶτος.g: the back of men or animals
νῶτος.as:
νῶτος, -ου, ὁ,
in Att. most freq. τὸ νῶτον, and in pl. always τὰ νῶτα, [in LXX, ὁ ν., pl., οἱ νῶτοι, and τὰ νῶτα, chiefly for כָּתֵף, also for עֹרֶף, מָתְנַיִם;]
the back: Ro 11:10(LXX).†

Νάρκισσος.der: a flower of the same name, from (stupefaction, as a "narcotic");

Νηρεύς.der: apparently from a derivative of the base of G3491 (ναῦς) (meaning wet);

νουθεσία.sd: calling attention to, i.e. (by implication) mild rebuke or warning
νουθεσία.der: from G3563 (νοῦς) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
νουθεσία.as:
** νουθεσία, -ας ἡ
(< νουθετέω), = cl. νουθέτησις; [in LXX: Wi 16:6*;]
admonition: I Co 10:11, Eph 6:4, Tit 3:10 (Aristoph., Diod., al.).†

νηπιάζω.sd: to act as a babe, i.e. (figuratively) innocently
νηπιάζω.as:
* νηπιάζω
(< νήπιος), (Hippocr., = νηπιαχεύω, Hom.),
to be a babe: I Co 14:20.†

νή.long: of affirmative swearing: by, with acc. of person or thing sworn by.
νή.sd: a particle of attestation (accompanied by the object invoked or appealed to in confirmation); as sure as
νή.der: probably an intensive form of G3483 (ναί);
νή.as:
νή,
particle of affirmation employed in oaths,
[in LXX: ν. τ. ὑγίειαν, Ge 42:15, 16 (חֵי)*;]
by: c. acc., I Co 15:31.†

νόημα.long: a thought, purpose, design; the mind; the heart, soul, feelings.
νόημα.sd: a perception, i.e. purpose, or (by implication) the intellect, disposition, itself
νόημα.as:
** νόημα, -τος, τό
(νοέω), [in LXX: Si 21:11, Ba 2:8, III Mac 5:30*;]
athought, purpose, design: II Co 2:1110:511:3, Phl 4:7. Meton., of the mind, II Co 3:144:4.†

ναυαγέω.long: (a) I am shipwrecked; so (b) fig: I come to ruin.
ναυαγέω.sd: to be shipwrecked (stranded, "navigate"), literally or figuratively
ναυαγέω.der: from a compound of G3491 (ναῦς) and G71 (ἄγω);
ναυαγέω.as:
* ναυαγέω, -ῶ
(< ναῦς, + ἄγνυμι, to break),
to suffer shipwreck: II Co 11:25; metaph., seq. περὶ τ. πίστιν, I Ti 1:19.†

νυχθήμερον.long: a night and day, twenty-four hours.
νυχθήμερον.sd: a day-and-night, i.e. full day of twenty-four hours
νυχθήμερον.as:
*† νυχθήμερος, -α, -ον
(< νύξ, ἡμέρα, v. B1., § 28, 4),
lasting a night and a day; as subst., (τὸ) ν., a night and a day: II Co 11:25 (pl., Or. Sib., 8, 203).†

νουμηνία.g: the new moon as a festival
νουμηνία.long: the new moon, first of the month.
νουμηνία.der: feminine of a compound of G3501 (νέος) and G3376 (μήν) (as noun by implication, of G2250 (ἡμέρα));

Νύμφα.der: probably contracted for a compound of G3565 (νύμφη) and G1435 (δῶρον);
Νύμφα.as:
Νύμφα (Rec., R, txt., Νυμφᾶς, q.v.), -ης, ἡ,
Nympha (v. M, Pr., 48): Col 4:15, WH, R, mg.†

νήφω.long: (lit: I am sober), I am calm (vigilant), circumspect.
νήφω.sd: to abstain from wine (keep sober), i.e. (figuratively) be discreet
νήφω.as:
* νήφω,
to be sober, abstain from wine; metaph., of moral alertness, to be sober, calm, circumspect: I Th 5:68, II Ti 4:5 (v. Ellic., in l.), I Pe 1:134:75:8 (cf. ἀνα-, ἐκ-νήφω, and v. MM, xvii).†
SYN.: ἀγρυπνέω, γρηγορέω.

νομίμως.sd: legitimately (specially, agreeably to the rules of the lists)
νομίμως.der: adverb from a derivative of G3551 (νόμος);
νομίμως.as:
** νομίμως,
adv.
(< νόμιμος, conformable to law), [in LXX: IV Mac 6:18*;]
rightly, lawfully: I Ti 1:8, II Ti 2:5.†

νηφάλιος.long: sober, not intoxicated (with wine), temperate, vigilant.
νηφάλιος.as:
* νηφάλιος (-λεος, Rec., in I Ti 3:2, 11), -ον (in cl., -α, -ον),
(< νήφω),
1. in cl., of drink, not mixed with wine.
2. In later writers (Plut., al.), of persons, sober, temperate: I Ti 3:2, 11, Tit 2:2.†

νεόφυτος.long: (lit: newly-planted), newly converted to Christianity, recent convert.
νεόφυτος.sd: newly planted, i.e. (figuratively) a young convert ("neophyte")
νεόφυτος.der: from G3501 (νέος) and a derivative of G5453 (φύω);
νεόφυτος.as:
νεό-φυτος, -ον
(< νέος, φύω), [in LXX: Jb 14:9, Ps 143 (144):12, Is 5:7 (נֶטַע), Ps 127 (128):3 (שְׁתִיל)*;]
newly planted (LXX). Metaph., as subst., ὁ ν., a new convert, neophyte, novice: I Ti 3:6.†

νοσέω.long: I am diseased, hence of mental or spiritual disease.
νοσέω.sd: to be sick, i.e. (by implication, of a diseased appetite) to hanker after (figuratively, to harp upon)
νοσέω.as:
** νοσέω, -ῶ
(< νόσος), [in LXX (metaph.): Wi 17:8*;]
to be sick: metaph., of mental ailment, seq. περί, I Ti 6:4 (cf. Plat., Mor., 546 d).†

νεωτερικός.sd: appertaining to younger persons, i.e. juvenile
νεωτερικός.as:
**† νεωτερικός, -ή, -όν
(< νεώτερος), [in LXX: III Mac 4:8*;]
= νεανικός, youthful, esp. of qualities: ἐπιθυμίαι, II Ti 2:22 (Polyb.).†

Νικόπολις.sd: victorious city; Nicopolis, a place in Macedonia
Νικόπολις.as:
Νικόπολις, -εως, ἡ,
Nicopolis, prob. the city of that name in Epirus (CGT, in l.): Tit 3:12.†

νωθρός.long: blunt, dull, hence spiritually; sluggish, remiss, slack.
νωθρός.as:
νωθρός, -ά, -όν,
[in LXX: Pr 22:29 (חָשֹׁךְ), Si 4:2911:12*;]
sluggish, slothful: He 5:116:12 (for similar usage in π., v. MM, xvii).
SYN.: ἀργός (q.v.), βραδύς.

νομοθετέομαι.long: (a) I ordain, lay down, give the sanction of law to, enact, (b) I base legally, regulate, direct.
νομοθετέομαι.sd: to legislate, i.e. (passively) to have (the Mosaic) enactments injoined, be sanctioned (by them)
νομοθετέομαι.as:
νομοθετέω, -ῶ,
[in LXX for ירה hi.;]
1. intrans., to make laws; pass., to be furnished with laws: He 7:11.
2. Trans., to ordain by law, enact: pass., He 8:6.†

νέφος.long: a cloud; met: a dense crowd, a multitude, great company.
νέφος.as:
νέφος, -ους, τό,
[in LXX for עָב, שַׁחַק, עָנָן;]
a mass of clouds, a cloud (cf. νεφέλη); metaph. (as in Hom., Hdt., al.), of a dense throng: He 12:1.†

νόθος.as:
** νόθος, -η, -ον,
[in LXX: Wi 4:3*;]
a bastard, base born, i.e. born of a slave or concubine: He 12:8.†

νομοθέτης.der: from G3551 (νόμος) and a derivative of G5087 (τίθημι);
νομοθέτης.as:
νομο-θέτης, -ου, ὁ
(< νόμος, τίθημι), [in LXX: Ps 9:20*;]
a lawgiver: Ja 4:12.†

νίκη.sd: conquest (abstractly), i.e. (figuratively) the means of success
νίκη.as:
νίκη, -ης, ἡ,
[in LXX: I Ch 29:11 (נֵצַח), freq. in I-IV Mac;]
victory: I Jo 5:4.†

Νικολαΐτης.long: a Nicolaitan, possibly a follower of Nicolaus (a heretic at Ephesus).
Νικολαΐτης.sd: a Nicolaite, i.e. adherent of Nicolaus
Νικολαΐτης.as:
Νικολαΐτης, -αυ, ὁ,
a Nicolaitan: pl., Re 2:6, 15.†

νεφρός.g: a kidney as a general emotional center
νεφρός.long: a kidney (as a general emotional center), the reins.
νεφρός.sd: a kidney (plural), i.e. (figuratively) the inmost mind
νεφρός.as:
νεφρός, -οῦ, ὁ,
[in LXX for כִּלְיָה, Ex 29:13, al.; metaph., Ps 7:915 (16):725 (26):2, Wi 1:6, al.;]
a kidney; pl., the kidneys, reins; metaph., of the will and affections: ν. καί καρδίαι (thoughts), Re 2:23.†
